mainTopic: Lashes for a נזיר whose days are complete; overlapping נזירות for a son, and רב's rule that one day counts for two terms
overview: The גמרא finishes the discussion of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, who said a נזיר whose days are complete is lashed only for טומאה. It explains that טומאה is special because of a פסוק. Then a ברייתא says he is lashed for wine, shaving and טומאה alike, so his view is refuted (תיובתא). A new משנה follows: a man vowed to be a נזיר when he has a son, and also took on a 100-day נזירות. If the son is born up to day seventy he loses nothing, but after seventy the seventy days are cancelled, because a תגלחת needs at least thirty days. רב rules that day seventy counts for both terms. The גמרא tests this against the משנה and concludes that the משנה disagrees with רב. It then asks whose view רב follows. It suggests אבא שאול and begins quoting a source about mourning cut short by a רגל; the source continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why impurity is different: the head-dependent נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why a נזיר whose days are done can still be lashed for טומאה: the פסוק 'וטמא ראש נזרו' includes someone whose נזירות now depends only on his head.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is different, because the Torah says: 'And he makes his נזיר-head impure.' This includes someone whose נזירות depends only on his head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why טומאה is treated differently from wine and shaving for a נזיר whose days are already over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine and shaving are not punished once the days are complete, according to רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא. טומאה is still punished because the פסוק says 'ראש נזרו', his נזיר-head. That wording covers a person whose only remaining נזירות is the shaving of his head.

keyTerms.meaning: And he makes his נזיר-head impure

phrases.english: Here it is different
for the Merciful One said: 'And he makes his נזיר-head impure,'
meaning one whose נזירות depends only on his head.
phrases.notes: He means a נזיר whose days are over and who only still has to shave his head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from earlier on the daf about why טומאה differs from wine and shaving in רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural distinction: a special פסוק covers טומאה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once the days are done, maybe no prohibition carries מלקות anymore, טומאה included.
steps.terutzMaskana: טומאה is still lashed, because 'ראש נזרו' includes a נזיר whose נזירות hangs only on his head.

steps.title: A ברייתא says he is lashed for all three
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: a נזיר whose days are done is forbidden to shave, drink wine and become impure, and he gets forty lashes for any of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: A נזיר whose days are complete is forbidden to shave, to drink wine and to become impure from the dead. If he shaved, drank wine or became impure from the dead, he receives the forty lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that goes against רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said that after the days are complete there are no lashes for wine or shaving. The ברייתא lists all three prohibitions together and gives forty lashes for each one. That clearly contradicts him.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
A נזיר whose days are complete
is forbidden to shave and to drink wine
and to become impure from the dead.
And if he shaved, or drank wine,
or became impure from the dead,
he receives the forty lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the whole position that step 1 was defending.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's ruling that a נזיר whose days are complete is not lashed for wine or shaving.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly gives forty lashes for shaving, wine and טומאה alike after the days are complete.

steps.title: The view is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the ברייתא is a full refutation of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא declares that רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's view is rejected, because no answer to the ברייתא is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'תיובתא' means the challenge stands and the opinion falls. The halacha follows the ברייתא: after the days are complete, a נזיר is still lashed for all three prohibitions.
steps.whatToRemember: A נזיר whose days are over but who has not yet shaved is still lashed for wine, shaving and טומאה. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's view is refuted.

phrases.english: This is a conclusive refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of step 2 with no answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא stands: a נזיר whose days are complete is lashed for wine, shaving and טומאה.

steps.title: משנה: a son born during a 100-day נזירות
steps.stepSummary: A man took on נזירות for when he has a son, plus a 100-day נזירות. If the son is born by day seventy, he loses nothing. If the son is born after day seventy, the seventy days are lost, because a תגלחת cannot come after fewer than thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man said, 'I am a נזיר when I have a son,' and also, 'a נזיר for a hundred days,' and a son was born to him up to day seventy, he loses nothing. After seventy, the seventy days are cancelled, because there is no shaving after fewer than thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה presents a case of two overlapping נזירות vows. It explains when the days already kept still count and when they are lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the son is born, he stops the 100-day נזירות and keeps the son's thirty-day נזירות, then shaves. If at least thirty days are left of the hundred, he finishes them and shaves again, so nothing is lost. If fewer than thirty are left, he cannot end with a shaving after so few days, so the first seventy are cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: The shaving at the end of נזירות

steps.confusionAlert: 'Up to seventy' is about how many days of the 100 he has already kept. The key point is whether at least thirty days are still left for him to keep after the son's נזירות.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a basic rule of נזירות: every תגלחת must come after a stretch of at least thirty days.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
'I am hereby a נזיר when I will have a son,'
and 'a נזיר for one hundred days,'
phrases.notes: He means he started the hundred days right away.

phrases.english: if a son was born to him up to day seventy,
he has not lost anything.
After seventy, it cancels the seventy.
For there is no shaving after fewer than thirty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר לִכְשֶׁיְּהֵא לִי בֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה after the previous discussion has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A son born by day seventy of a 100-day נזירות causes no loss. A son born after day seventy cancels the seventy days, since a תגלחת cannot follow fewer than thirty days.

steps.title: רב: The seventieth day counts for both terms
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that day seventy counts both for the 100-day נזירות and for the son's נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The seventieth day counts for here and for there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling from רב about the משנה's case. If the son is born on day seventy, that one day counts for both נזירות terms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Day seventy finishes the seventy days of his 100-day term. The same day also starts his נזירות for the son, so one day does double duty.

keyTerms.meaning: An early אמורא whose ruling is being discussed
The seventieth day of the 100-day נזירות
Counts for this and for that (for both terms)

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav said:
The seventieth day counts for here and for there.
phrases.notes: "Here and there" means the 100-day נזירות and the נזירות for his son.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: יוֹם שִׁבְעִים עוֹלֶה לְכָאן וּלְכָאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an אמורא's ruling about the exact day seventy in the משנה's case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Day seventy counts both as the end of the first seventy days and as the first day of the son's נזירות.

steps.title: The משנה says he only 'loses nothing', but by רב he gains
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that if the son is born by day seventy he 'loses nothing'. According to רב, he should actually gain a day.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: If a son is born to him up to seventy, he has not lost anything. But if you think the day counts for both, then he actually gains!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב from the first part of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Up to seventy' sounds like it includes day seventy itself. If that day counts twice, he does better than just 'losing nothing', because he saves a day. So the משנה should not describe it as merely not losing.

keyTerms.meaning: If it enters your mind (if you think)

phrases.english: We learned:
If a son is born to him up to seventy,
he has not lost anything.
And if it enters your mind
that it counts for here and for there,
he actually gains!
phrases.notes: He saves a day, because one day is counted twice.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: נוֹלַד לוֹ עַד שִׁבְעִים — לֹא הִפְסִיד כְּלוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's ruling from the wording of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that day seventy counts for both terms
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If day seventy counts twice, a son born on that day brings a gain. The משנה should not then call it merely 'not losing'.

steps.title: The mishnah's wording mirrors its last clause
steps.stepSummary: The משנה only said 'up to seventy' to match the contrast with the סיפא, 'after seventy'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, by right it should not have taught 'up to seventy'. But because the last clause teaches 'after seventy it cancels seventy', the first clause teaches 'seventy'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by explaining that the משנה's wording is not exact here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Strictly speaking, the משנה should not have written 'up to seventy loses nothing', since on day seventy itself he gains. It used the word 'seventy' to set up a neat contrast with the סיפא, where 'after seventy' causes a loss.

keyTerms.meaning: The last clause of the משנה
The first clause of the משנה

phrases.english: Rather, by right
it should not have taught "up to seventy,"
but because the last clause teaches
"after seventy, it cancels seventy,"
the first clause teaches "seventy."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּדִין הוּא דְּלָא לִיתְנֵי עַד שִׁבְעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the רישא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the משנה's wording as stylistic, chosen to parallel the סיפא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's 'up to seventy, loses nothing' is exact and includes day seventy
steps.terutzMaskana: The wording 'seventy' in the רישא was chosen only to contrast with the סיפא, so רב's rule stands

steps.title: Challenge from the last clause: after seventy cancels seventy
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא says a son born after seventy cancels the seventy days. With רב's double counting, there should be enough days left.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear from the last clause: If the son is born after seventy, it cancels the seventy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge to רב, this time from the סיפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the son is born on day seventy-one, after seventy full days of the 100. By רב's rule, the last day of the son's thirty-day term also counts toward the 100. That still leaves a full thirty days of growth before the final תגלחת, so why should the seventy days be lost?

keyTerms.meaning: Cancels, makes him lose the days already counted

phrases.english: Come and hear from the last clause:
If he is born after seventy,
it cancels seventy.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע מִסֵּיפָא: נוֹלַד אַחַר שִׁבְעִים — סוֹתֵר שִׁבְעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the רישא challenge was answered, a new challenge comes from the סיפא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With double counting, a son born on day seventy-one still leaves thirty days of growth. So the seventy days should not be cancelled.

steps.title: 'After' means two days after
steps.stepSummary: 'After seventy' in the משנה means 'after, after', meaning day seventy-two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading 'after seventy' as the second day after seventy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the son is born on day seventy-two, even with double counting there are fewer than thirty days left. A תגלחת cannot come after fewer than thirty days, so the seventy days are lost. Day seventy-one works out like day seventy and causes no loss.

keyTerms.meaning: After, after: the second day after seventy

steps.whatToRemember: For now, the גמרא reads 'after' in the סיפא as day seventy-two to keep the משנה in line with רב. Step 11 attacks this reading, and Step 12 rejects it.
steps.confusionAlert: This reading of 'after' as day seventy-two is only a temporary defense of רב. In Steps 10-12 the גמרא rejects it and concludes that 'after' means day seventy-one.

phrases.english: What is "after"?
After, after.
phrases.notes: He means the day after the day after seventy, which is day seventy-two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the סיפא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads a word in the משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: 'After seventy' means day seventy-two, so רב's double counting still fits the משנה

steps.title: What happens if the son is born on day seventy-one?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about a son born on day seventy-one: according to רב, would that birth also not cancel the earlier days?
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about a son born on the very next day, day seventy-one? According to רב, would that also not cancel the earlier days?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is testing the answer from Step 9 by asking about day seventy-one. It is setting up a challenge that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said 'after seventy' means day seventy-two. That leaves day seventy-one unexplained. With רב's double counting, day seventy-one still leaves thirty days, so it should not cancel the earlier days either.

keyTerms.meaning: Cancels, wipes out the days already counted

phrases.english: But what about the actual day after?
phrases.notes: He means day seventy-one, the very next day after seventy.

phrases.english: Is it so too, that it does not cancel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Probes the gap left by Step 9's reading of 'after' as day seventy-two.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the law, according to רב, if the son is born on day seventy-one?

steps.title: Then the משנה should have included day seventy-one
steps.stepSummary: If day seventy-one does not cancel anything, the משנה should not have drawn its line at 'up to seventy'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the משנה say only that a son born up to day seventy causes no loss? Even a son born after seventy, on day seventy-one, causes no loss, since you said it does not cancel!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the question from Step 10 into a full challenge. If day seventy-one is also safe, the משנה put its dividing line in the wrong place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה draws a clear line: up to seventy causes no loss, and after seventy cancels the days. According to רב, the safe zone should reach day seventy-one. So the משנה's wording does not match רב's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this case? (it seems to apply more widely)

phrases.english: If so, why specifically
does it teach: 'born up to seventy'
'he lost nothing'?
Even after seventy as well!
Didn't you say it does not cancel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the question of Step 10 into a challenge against the answer of Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of Step 9, that 'after seventy' means day seventy-two
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If day seventy-one also causes no loss, the משנה's line at 'up to seventy' is in the wrong place. The משנה should have said 'up to seventy-one'.

steps.title: 'After' means day seventy-one, so the משנה does not fit רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that 'after seventy' means day seventy-one, and so the משנה does not fit רב's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this that 'after' means the actual next day. And so the משנה is a difficulty for רב. Learn from it that this is so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the answer from Step 9 and concludes that the משנה does not agree with רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the משנה treats day seventy-one as cancelling the earlier days, it does not count one day for two נזירות periods. So the תנא of the משנה disagrees with רב. This opens the question of whose view רב is following.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (a conclusion is being drawn)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה reads 'after seventy' as day seventy-one. That means the משנה does not accept רב's idea that one day can count for two נזירות periods.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this: 'after' means the actual next day.
And so, the משנה is a difficulty for רב.
phrases.notes: The words 'is a difficulty' are not written here, but the גמרא assumes them.

phrases.english: Learn from it that this is so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of Step 11 and closes the whole cycle that began in Step 6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'After seventy' in the משנה means day seventy-one, so the משנה disagrees with רב's double-counting ruling.

steps.title: Whose opinion is רב following?
steps.stepSummary: Since the משנה disagrees with רב, the גמרא asks which תנא's opinion רב based his ruling on.
steps.simpleTranslation: And whose opinion was רב following when he said his ruling?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new search for an earlier authority who agrees with רב. This sets up the suggestion in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא like רב normally needs a תנא to support him. The משנה's תנא just turned out to disagree with him, so the גמרא looks for some other תנא who holds that one day can count for two things.

phrases.english: And רב, according to whom
did he say his ruling?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from Step 12: the משנה does not support רב, so the גמרא looks for another source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds, like רב, that one day can count toward two separate periods?

steps.title: Suggestion: רב follows אבא שאול on mourning before a רגל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב follows אבא שאול. It starts quoting a source: someone who buries a relative three days before a רגל is freed from the rest of the seven days of mourning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose we say רב follows אבא שאול. As we learned: someone who buries his dead relative three days before a רגל is freed from the decree of seven days of mourning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first guess that רב follows אבא שאול, and it begins quoting the source where אבא שאול's view appears. The quote continues past this point, so this is still being set up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a mourner whose seven days of mourning are cut short by a רגל. The גמרא is about to compare this to רב's idea that one day can do double duty. The word 'אילימא' ('if we say') hints that this suggestion may be questioned.

keyTerms.meaning: If we say (a suggestion that may be rejected)
The rabbinic rule of seven days of mourning
As we learned (introduces a quoted source)

steps.confusionAlert: The quote is not finished here. The next step continues the same source, and אבא שאול's own words come only after that, on the next amud. So do not decide yet how this supports רב's view.

phrases.english: If we say like אבא שאול, as we learned:
One who buries his dead relative
three days before a pilgrimage festival:
the decree of seven days is cancelled for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first suggested answer to the question of Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A tentative answer: רב may follow אבא שאול, based on the source about mourning cut short by a רגל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A source about a mourner who buries his relative three days before a רגל

steps.title: Burial eight days before a festival cancels the thirty days
steps.stepSummary: The source continues. If the burial was eight days before a רגל, the רגל cancels the thirty-day mourning rules (גזירת שלשים). So he may cut his hair on ערב הרגל. If he did not, he may not cut it after the רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he buried his relative eight days before a רגל, the thirty-day mourning rule no longer applies to him. He may cut his hair on the day before the רגל. But if he did not cut it then, he may not cut it after the רגל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the source it began in Step 14 to show who רב follows. This line adds a second case: burial eight days before the רגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eight days means he finished the seven days of שבעה and also kept one day of שלשים. Because he already started שלשים, the רגל cancels the rest of it, just as the earlier case said the רגל cancels the rest of שבעה. The cancellation only helps him if he uses it. If he skipped the haircut before the רגל, the haircut ban comes back after the רגל.

keyTerms.meaning: The rules of the thirty-day mourning period, such as not cutting hair
Is cancelled for him; it no longer applies

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the רגל simply ends שלשים no matter what. He gets permission to cut his hair before the רגל. If he doesn't use it then, he cannot cut it afterward until the thirty days are over.

phrases.english: If he buried his relative eight days before a festival,
phrases.notes: "Buried his relative" isn't written here. It carries over from the first case in Step 14, which was three days before the festival.

phrases.english: the decree of the thirty days is cancelled for him.
And he is permitted to cut his hair on the eve of the festival.
But if he did not cut his hair on the eve of the festival,
he is forbidden to cut his hair after the festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמֹנָה יָמִים קוֹדֶם לָרֶגֶל בָּטְלָה מִמֶּנּוּ גְּזֵירַת שְׁלֹשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the source begun in Step 14, adding the case of eight days and the thirty-day period.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא does רב follow (from Step 13)?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source being quoted for אבא שאול's view continues. Burial eight days before a רגל lets the רגל cancel שלשים, and the haircut permission applies only on ערב הרגל.
